activities.anchor: the most productive single-case study in neuroscience
activities.caption: file each outcome — preserved or lost in H.M.
activities.name: mcHmBuckets

config.prompt: After Scoville's 1953 resection, Henry Molaison's abilities split. File each outcome:

items.label: improving at mirror-drawing across days of practice
most memories from the decade preceding the surgery
the ability to keep each practice session from feeling brand-new

config.why: The split founded the multiple-systems doctrine: working memory is prefrontal-parietal, skills run on basal ganglia and cerebellum, and the hippocampus is a writer whose entries are eventually filed elsewhere.

activities.anchor: Kandel's gamble was that molecular logic
activities.caption: rebuild the chain — from sensitisation to long-term memory
activities.name: mcKandelOrder

config.prompt: The sea slug taught the field the molecular half of memory. Rebuild the chain:
items: A noxious stimulus sensitises the gill-withdrawal reflex — non-associative learning
Serotonin is released from a modulatory neuron onto a particular sensory-motor synapse
cAMP and protein kinases increase transmitter release at that synapse
CREB-dependent transcription converts short-lasting plasticity into protein-synthesis-dependent long-term memory
config.why: The same molecular logic generalises up the evolutionary tree — flies, mice and humans — which is why the gamble earned the 2000 Nobel.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the LTP mechanism
activities.name: mcLtpSpot

config.prompt: A worked summary of LTP at CA3-to-CA1 synapses contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: A high-frequency tetanus leaves transmission potentiated for hours.
Glutamate is bound and the postsynaptic membrane depolarises — the magnesium block lifts.
Calcium enters and activates kinases such as CaMKII.
CaMKII removes AMPA receptors from the postsynaptic density, so the synapse conducts less.
Late LTP additionally requires CREB-driven protein synthesis.
config.correction: CaMKII inserts additional AMPA receptors into the postsynaptic density — the synapse becomes physically bigger and conductively stronger, not weaker.
config.why: Early potentiation is receptor trafficking lasting hours; late LTP needs gene expression — and blocking protein synthesis in the window erases only the long-term component.

activities.caption: place the marker — the size of the sleep bonus
activities.name: mcSleepPlace

config.prompt: In classic paradigms, sleep after learning improves retention. Place the marker at the middle of the measured range:
config.why: The classic range is 20–40% better retention — and sleep deprivation after learning measurably impairs consolidation, while targeted memory reactivation selectively boosts cued memories.

activities.anchor: Staying awake feels like protecting study hours
activities.caption: the night before the exam — decide
activities.name: mcNightBranch

config.root: The exam is at 9 a.m. The textbook is still open. Decide:

start.text: How do you spend the night?

choices.label: Cancel sleep — every hour rereading is an hour of studying
choices.feedback: Staying awake feels like protecting study hours, but consolidation is work the brain performs mainly during slow-wave sleep.

choices.label: Learn, sleep, then retrieve in the morning
choices.feedback: Hippocampal replays inside sharp-wave ripples teach cortex — the night is part of the studying.

allnighter.text: Sleep deprivation after learning measurably impairs retention: the replays never run, so the cortical dialogue that files the trace is missed. The all-nighter is self-sabotage.

schedule.text: Consolidation is work the brain performs mainly during slow-wave sleep: learn, sleep, then retrieve — the schedule that hands the trace its best chance.

config.why: Targeted memory reactivation — cueing a learned association with its odour or sound during sleep — selectively boosts the cued memories: the night shift is real.

activities.anchor: For decades retrieval was assumed passive
activities.caption: drag the divider — the file-cabinet and the rewrite
activities.name: mcRecallCompare

config.prompt: Two views of what happens at the moment of recall. Drag the divider:

before.label: Storage view
before.text: Retrieval reads the file: recall is passive playback of a trace stored unchanged since encoding.

after.label: Constructive view
after.text: Each retrieval returns the trace to a labile state and re-files it with current context and emotion attached — recall is rewriting. Misinformation effects and reconsolidation-window therapies both ride on this.

config.why: Nader, Schafe and LeDoux (2000) settled it: a protein-synthesis inhibitor blocked restabilisation only when given during the window after recall.

activities.caption: pair each case with what it revealed
activities.name: mcAmygdalaMatch

config.prompt: The emotional side of the memory systems. Pair each finding with its meaning:

pairs.right: no fear conditioning, no recognition of fearful faces — other memory systems intact

pairs.left: conditioned responses to stimuli the patient denies seeing
pairs.right: affective processing can run without reportable experience
confidence rose over years while accuracy fell

config.why: Emotional arousal strengthens consolidation via amygdala-norepinephrine-hippocampus interactions — vividness and confidence track arousal, not accuracy.

activities.caption: which curve matches arousal against memory?
activities.name: mcArousalTrace

config.prompt: Emotional arousal modulates consolidation. Which curve matches memory performance as arousal rises from none to extreme?

curves.label: rises to a peak, then falls

config.why: The Yerkes-Dodson inverted-U: moderate arousal enhances memory, while extreme stress impairs encoding and retrieval — the prefrontal shut-down of trauma.
